items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: Jack Paidi playing trumpet... when he come back to the band, to his band... I was at the dance that night. They done hired Sam Morgan in his place... Jack Paeda got sick there... I played dance. You take Jack Paeda, Son, and Thomas.

ctx.x: I don't remember, he and his father, and his brother, what is his name? Johnny Lindsay, eh? Good ass. But didn't Jack Paidi play with Johnny? No Johnny Lindsay band? Johnny Lindsay, I don't know. But I know. You know Johnny Lindsay?

In my time, I had Bill Beating Drum, Yank On Trambone. You take, uh... Oh, that boy, he died down there earlier. Julius Granderson playing banjo. I forget who was playing bass. Jack Paidi playing trumpet. Cause his team song, I'll never forget that. Cause I just was getting big enough then. I was around 20 years old then. His team song, If You Don't Like The Way I Do. Yeah. You understand? That was his team song. Cause I was like, you know, I was like, you know. You know what I was like? You know what I was like?…
They put him out of his own band.

items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Jack Paeda was playing trumpet in the band across there... that's why he made the band up, Sam Morgan's band. Yeah, and I was the first one to start him to cross the lake.

ctx.x: It's always there that I played. I took his place.

And so Sam Morgan, he was playing in the hall across the river there. And Sam Morgan, he stole the Isaiah. Let me see how that thing was. I believe it was Sam. Sam Morgan, Jack Paeda was playing trumpet in the band across there and Sam Morgan, he went over there. He got sick. Jack Paeda got sick. Sam Morgan, he went over there in his place and hid him over his face. So when he got better they find him. And that's why he made the band up, Sam Morgan's band.
